title: Sticky WhatsApp contact patterns — Mobbin research

method.source: Mobbin search_sections and search_screens, with visual review of returned images

queries.query: A floating WhatsApp contact button or WhatsApp chat bar pinned to the bottom corner of a website
A floating contact bar at the bottom of a website with a contact us button and a short invitation to start a project
A website with a sticky bottom bar containing contact, chat or message actions
A website landing page with a small floating live chat support launcher button in the bottom right corner
A floating pill navigation bar centered at the bottom of a website with a contact button
A product details page with a floating bottom call to action bar containing a primary booking or contact button
A public website page with a floating customer support chat launcher button or chat with us tab at the bottom right corner
A website hero with a floating bottom navigation dock and a let's talk contact call to action
A compact live chat tab labeled chat with us or help at the bottom edge of a website
A customer support page with a button to contact the business on WhatsApp

method.limits: Screenshots establish visible composition, not scroll persistence, responsive behavior, live availability or conversion performance. Most references are adjacent chat and CTA patterns. Base44 shows an explicit WhatsApp handoff, but not a sticky bar.

recommendation: Compare a green icon-and-label contact pill based on Mailchimp with a mobile bottom contact bar based on Kiwi. Preserve the confirmed WhatsApp destination, palette-charcoal mark and generous padding. These are proposals for review.

references.name: Mailchimp
references.observed: A dark rounded pill with a speech icon and “Chat with us” sits at the lower-right edge.
references.takeaway: Best starting point for adding a short Hebrew label beside the WhatsApp mark.
references.tradeoff: Wider than the current circle; check it against the showreel and narrow viewports.

references.name: ExpressVPN
references.observed: A compact green “Need help? Chat with us!” tab sits along the lower-right edge, separate from the large support section.
references.takeaway: A text label makes the contact purpose explicit while leaving most of the page clear.
references.tradeoff: The captured tab is small and flush to the edge; increase its touch target and safe-area spacing for Moriz.
references.evidence: Website capture; persistence while scrolling is unverified.

references.name: Intercom
references.observed: A blue circular chat launcher sits in the bottom-right corner beside the article layout.
references.takeaway: Compare the compact footprint with Moriz’s existing green circle.
references.tradeoff: An icon alone says less about who will answer or which channel opens.
references.evidence: Website capture; no WhatsApp integration shown.

references.name: Kiwi.com
references.observed: A white rounded strip sits across the bottom of a form, containing a wide green payment action.
references.takeaway: Study the bar’s separation from page content and the strong single action; adapt the destination and label to WhatsApp.
references.tradeoff: A full-width bar occupies more vertical space and can cover project media.
references.evidence: Booking/payment interface; transferable geometry, not a contact or WhatsApp example.

references.name: Hers
references.observed: A slim white strip at the bottom pairs product information with a dark action on the right.
references.takeaway: Compare a short invitation plus one WhatsApp action inside a restrained horizontal strip.
references.tradeoff: Long Hebrew text could make the strip too tall; test wrapping and content clearance.
references.evidence: Commerce interface; visible bottom strip, not a WhatsApp implementation.

references.name: Base44
references.observed: A WhatsApp heading and green “Open WhatsApp” button appear in a connection card.
references.takeaway: Use the channel name and icon to make the transition out of the website clear.
references.tradeoff: This is an account-connection flow with activation instructions; those steps do not belong in Moriz’s direct contact link.
references.evidence: Actual WhatsApp action visible; static card, not a sticky bar.

references.name: Loops
references.observed: A conversation panel occupies the lower-right corner; its header shows a person’s initials, name and close control.
references.takeaway: Useful if comparing a compact invitation that introduces Mor before handing off to WhatsApp.
references.tradeoff: A panel adds an interaction step and covers content; a direct link is simpler.
references.evidence: Authenticated support interface; expanded state, not a WhatsApp handoff.

references.name: Navan
references.observed: A support conversation panel sits on the left over a travel page, with minimize and close controls.
references.takeaway: Study the left-edge placement when comparing the Hebrew RTL contact control.
references.tradeoff: The panel covers a large portion of the page; placement is a design choice, not automatically dictated by RTL.
references.evidence: Authenticated travel interface; expanded chat state.

references.name: Klook
references.observed: A centered chat panel combines a colored header, topic-choice buttons and a message field.
references.takeaway: A reference for comparing a guided enquiry flow if Moriz later needs to qualify project requests.
references.tradeoff: This is substantially more complex than opening a WhatsApp conversation and is not a suitable default for the current control.
references.evidence: Expanded customer-support screen; centered, not a bottom contact bar.
